I farm 8 mu in a wheat-maize rotation, so I will put the full 8 mu into winter wheat first and then summer maize after wheat harvest. Because I have well irrigation, I will rely on water to keep both crops stable rather than gamble on rainfall. I have farmed for 30 years, so I do not want a complicated plan. I will use improved seed for wheat because it is steady and familiar, and hybrid seed for maize because I care about yield and it performs better for me in summer. I will keep fertilizer at a moderate-to-strong level since I need reliable grain from limited land and I also have a six-person household, with some labor going off-farm, so I want a plan that is productive but still manageable.

For wheat, I will do rotary tillage after the previous maize season and sow on time for the winter crop. I will give more nitrogen than phosphorus and potassium, with most of the nutrients supporting tillering and grain filling. I will irrigate several times because wheat in my area responds well to water at key stages. I will spray a few times if needed to control weeds and disease, but I will not overdo it. After wheat harvest, I will move directly into summer maize on the same 8 mu. I will use hybrid maize, keep rotary tillage for speed, apply solid nitrogen with supporting phosphorus and potassium, and irrigate enough to protect yield during the hot season. I will keep pesticide use moderate, mainly for weeds and insects. My goal is steady output from both crops with a practical workload I can handle.
